A markdown table is easy to read; a **database** is easy to *query*. Python's
standard library includes `sqlite3` — a whole SQL database in a single file, no
server — so a listener can record every run into a table you can later query for
trends, flaky tests, or slowest cases.

The pattern is the same v3 listener: open the database when the run starts,
insert a row per test, and commit when the run closes.

## Task 1 — Record each result into a table

**Goal:** create `ext/SqliteResults.py` — a v3 listener that creates a `results`
table in `results/results.db` and inserts each test's name and status.

Here is the same shape writing to a different table — one keyed by tag. Adapt it
to store name and status.

<!-- example -->
```python
import sqlite3
import pathlib


class TagResults:
    ROBOT_LISTENER_API_VERSION = 3

    def __init__(self):
        pathlib.Path("results").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        self.db = sqlite3.connect("results/tags.db")
        self.db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tags (test TEXT, tag TEXT)")

    def end_test(self, data, result):
        for tag in data.tags:
            self.db.execute("INSERT INTO tags VALUES (?, ?)", (data.name, tag))

    def close(self):
        self.db.commit()
        self.db.close()
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `ext/SqliteResults.py` defines a listener that uses `sqlite3`.

<!-- hint -->
Open the database in `__init__` and create the table:
`self.db = sqlite3.connect("results/results.db")` then
`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS results (name TEXT, status TEXT)`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Insert in `end_test` — `INSERT INTO results VALUES (?, ?)`, `(data.name, result.status)` —
and `commit()` then `close()` in `close()`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```python
import sqlite3
import pathlib


class SqliteResults:
    ROBOT_LISTENER_API_VERSION = 3

    def __init__(self):
        pathlib.Path("results").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        self.db = sqlite3.connect("results/results.db")
        self.db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS results (name TEXT, status TEXT)")

    def end_test(self, data, result):
        self.db.execute("INSERT INTO results VALUES (?, ?)", (data.name, result.status))

    def close(self):
        self.db.commit()
        self.db.close()
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run the suite with your listener

```bash
uv run robot --listener ext/SqliteResults.py checks/orders.robot
```

`results/results.db` now holds a row per test. You could open it with any SQLite
tool and run `SELECT * FROM results;`.

> **Note:** If your test names carry non-ASCII characters, set
> `self.db.text_factory = str` right after connecting — otherwise SQLite can
> raise when it inserts them.

**Check:** `results/results.db` was created and contains the run's tests.
